name: Base
pitch: A plain, readable default theme with no strong identity, used when a deck names no theme or names one that doesn't exist.

name: Terminal
pitch: For infrastructure and live-coding talks where the audience lives in a shell and the deck should feel like one long tmux session.

name: Product
pitch: A launch-day talk for a developer tool, where every slide should feel like the landing page of something you want to install.

name: Swiss
pitch: An argument-driven engineering talk set like a Zurich concert poster: grid, grotesk, one red.

name: Newsprint
pitch: A war story or postmortem told as front-page news, where every slide is a headline and every number is a front-page figure.

name: Zine
pitch: An opinionated, scrappy talk with a point to argue: cut, pasted, and photocopied the night before, and proud of it.

name: Poster
pitch: For a loud, fast, opinionated talk in the Takahashi style, where every slide is a gig poster and the words do all the work.

name: Blueprint
pitch: For architecture and systems talks where every slide is a sheet from the drawing set and the diagrams are the argument.

name: Riso
pitch: A warm community-conference talk that should feel like a two-ink print pulled off the drum that morning.

name: Retro Computing
pitch: A nostalgic, slightly mischievous systems talk told from a 1990 desktop, where every idea opens in its own window.

name: Paperback
pitch: A story-led conference talk that wants the warmth and quiet authority of a mid-century paperback series.

name: Keynote
pitch: A big-room launch talk where one idea at a time lands on a dark stage, lit from above.

name: Editorial
pitch: A story-led talk told like a long-read magazine feature, with drop caps, pull quotes, and figures.

name: Observatory
pitch: A data-heavy infrastructure talk, charted like a night sky: systems as bodies, readings taken through a reticle.

name: Arcade
pitch: A high-energy war-story talk framed as a game you can win, built to stay legible on a washed-out projector.

name: Isometric
pitch: A friendly architecture walkthrough where the infrastructure itself is the cast: code, tables, and numbers become chunky little solids on a warm floor.

name: Ink
pitch: A calm, reflective talk about hard-won lessons, where each slide holds one thought and a lot of silence around it.

name: Lab Notebook
pitch: An evidence-first engineering talk where every claim arrives as a numbered figure and the speaker's red pen does the arguing.

name: Bauhaus
pitch: A bold, opinionated talk about first principles, where every idea is reduced to a circle, a triangle, or a square.

name: Sketch
pitch: For explainer talks that build an idea step by step, as if the speaker were drawing it on a whiteboard in front of you.

name: Transit
pitch: An architecture or infrastructure talk that walks the audience through a system the way a metro map walks a city.
